newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end off on Telebras, trade up.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end off on Telebras, trade up.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended slightly lower, led by speculative selling of Telebras ahead of Monday's options expiry, with trade rising as some investors began exercising options, brokers said.
"Many clients are exercising options," one dealer said, adding the sparring was between those holding Telebras options.

The Bovespa index of 49 most traded shares edged down 114 points, or 0.17 percent, to close at 66,335 points. Turnover was a hefty 536 million reais ($525.5 million), with options trade accounting for over half of volume.
Brokers said trade rose amid heightened options speculation ahead of settlements on Monday, with sparring between Telebras options holders with strikes prices at 80.00 reais and 84.00 reais.

The sellers -- those with options with the lower strike price -- gained the upper hand in the session, forcing Telebras shares down, they added. Telebras's benchmark preferred closed off 0.49 percent at 81.90 reais while its voting common declined 1.67 percent at 67.85 reais.
Investors were also nervous about Argentina's economic troubles and Brazil's poor September trade figures, they added.

Telebras' declines held back the market as some other leading shares gained on thin cash volume, led by a 5.15 percent rise in steelmaker Cia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN) to 23.50 reais. The stock benefited from the company's improving earnings outlook.

Petrobras also surged after news of an increase in its September oil inventory. The state oil monopoly's preferred jumped 3.64 percent to 128.00 reais while its voting common climbed 1.26 percent to 80.50 reais.
Electric utility stocks, which posted hefty gains recently on bright privatization prospects, rose slightly.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index (IEE) of the nine most-liquid power stocks edged up 0.06 percent to close at 1,793 despite profit-taking on leaders in the sector.
Investors booked profits on state power firm Eletrobras, whose common fell 1.21 percent to 326.00 reais while its preferred dropped 1.75 percent to end at 337.00 reais.
Minas Gerais state electrical firm Cemig slipped 0.59 percent to end at 33.80 reais.
State miner Cia Vale do Rio Doce preferred dipped 0.24 percent to end at 20.75 reais.
